findings.title: web/tsconfig.json does not extend the root tsconfig — 102 latent type errors are invisible in the frontend
findings.location: web/tsconfig.json:1 (no `extends`); cf. api/tsconfig.json:2 and shared/tsconfig.json:2 which both extend ../tsconfig.json
findings.evidence: Root tsconfig.json sets strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + noImplicitReturns + noFallthroughCasesInSwitch. api and shared inherit all four; web re-declares only `strict: true` standalone. `pnpm type-check` passes with 0 errors today. Running the same project with the three inherited flags restored: `tsc -p web/tsconfig.json --noEmit --noUncheckedIndexedAccess --noImplicitReturns --noFallthroughCasesInSwitch` => 102 errors (94 from noUncheckedIndexedAccess, 8 TS7030 from noImplicitReturns, 0 from noFallthroughCasesInSwitch). By code: 41 TS2532 'Object is possibly undefined', 29 TS18048, 12 TS2322, 11 TS2345, 1 TS18047. Densest: src/components/CommandPalette.tsx (13), src/lib/cn.ts (12), src/hooks/useSelection.ts (12), src/components/editor/CommentDisplay.tsx (12), src/components/editor/AIScoringDisplay.tsx (12). The repo's own reference config at research/configs/web/tsconfig.json DOES extend ../tsconfig.json — the shipped web config drifted from it.
findings.hypothesis: web/tsconfig.json was authored standalone for the Vite scaffold (moduleResolution: bundler, jsx, paths) instead of extending root and overriding those three fields, so the root's stricter flags were silently dropped for the one package with the most index/lookup-heavy code. Nobody noticed because `pnpm type-check` is green.
findings.estimatedImpact: Restoring inheritance and fixing the 102 errors converts the largest class of frontend runtime crash ('cannot read property of undefined' on array/record lookups) into compile errors. It also mechanically retires most of the 33 corrected web non-null assertions, because noUncheckedIndexedAccess forces real narrowing where `!` is currently used. Roughly 130 of the 1535 tracked violations (~8%) plus 102 previously-uncounted latent errors.

findings.title: The entire database-to-HTTP response path is implicitly `any` — 707 pg queries, none typed
findings.location: api/src/db/client.ts:43 (untyped `pool` export); api/src/routes/projects.ts:18, api/src/routes/projects.ts:1102, api/src/routes/weeks.ts:186, api/src/routes/weeks.ts:1793, api/src/routes/issues.ts:82, api/src/routes/programs.ts:12, api/src/routes/feedback.ts:27
findings.evidence: `@types/pg` declares `query<R extends QueryResultRow = any, I = any[]>(...)`, so an untyped call yields `QueryResult<any>` and `result.rows` is `any[]`. In api/src production code (excluding tests): 707 `pool|client|db.query(` call sites, 0 of which supply the generic type parameter, and 767 `.rows` member accesses. The only translation layer between those `any` rows and the JSON the frontend consumes is 7 hand-written mappers all declared `(row: any)`: extractProjectFromRow, extractSprintFromRow (x2, in projects.ts and weeks.ts), extractIssueFromRow, extractProgramFromRow, extractFeedbackFromRow, formatStandupResponse. Downstream consumers are also `any`: projects.ts:959-961 and :983-985 do `issuesResult.rows.filter((i: any) => i.state === 'done')`. Note this debt is largely invisible to the explicit-`any` counter — only the 7 mapper signatures and the `(i: any)` callbacks are annotated; the other ~760 row accesses are unannotated implicit `any` that `strict` cannot catch because the default generic is `any`.
findings.hypothesis: Deliberate 'no ORM, raw pg' choice (documented in the config as `dbLayer: raw pg Pool`) was adopted without the compensating step of declaring row interfaces per table/query. Because pg's generic defaults to `any` rather than `unknown`, opting out is the path of least resistance and strict mode never complains.
findings.estimatedImpact: This is the single largest unchecked surface in the codebase and sits directly on the API contract. A column rename or a `properties->>` key typo produces `undefined` in a JSON response with zero compile-time signal. Introducing per-query row interfaces and typing the 7 mappers removes ~40 explicit `any`s concentrated in the three densest production files and brings 767 previously-unchecked property accesses under the compiler.

findings.title: The Yjs <-> TipTap converter — the persistence path for every document's content — is fully untyped
findings.evidence: 12 explicit `any` in 245 lines — the densest production file in the repo by any-per-line. Every public signature is untyped: `yjsToJson(fragment: Y.XmlFragment): any`, `jsonToYjs(doc, fragment, content: any)`, `loadContentFromYjsState(yjsState: Buffer): any | null`, plus `extractTextWithMarks(el, inheritedMarks: any[]): any[]` and `yjsElementToJson(el): any[]`. Callers are on the core data path: api/src/collaboration/index.ts:118 calls `yjsToJson(fragment)` inside `persistDocument()` immediately before the result is written to `documents.content` and fed to extractHypothesis/SuccessCriteria/Vision/Goals extractors; api/src/routes/documents.ts:405 calls `loadContentFromYjsState(doc.yjs_state)` to serve document content over REST. api/src/types/y-protocols.d.ts adds 7 more `any` on the awareness/sync protocol surface these functions sit behind.
findings.hypothesis: ProseMirror/TipTap JSON is a recursive discriminated shape that nobody wanted to model by hand, and `@tiptap/core`'s JSONContent type is not imported on the API side (the api package has no TipTap dependency), so `any` was used as the interchange type on both directions of the conversion.
findings.estimatedImpact: Highest severity-per-line in the codebase: this is the only code that translates the collaborative CRDT state into the durable `content` column. A shape regression here corrupts or silently drops user-authored document content — the product's core artifact — and no type check would flag it. Modelling the node type (12 `any`s) is a small, high-value fix that also makes the four content-extractor utilities type-safe.

findings.title: 236 non-null assertions on request auth context, all traceable to one optional declaration
findings.location: api/src/middleware/auth.ts:11-12 (`userId?: string; workspaceId?: string;` on the Express Request augmentation); asserted at 236 call sites, e.g. api/src/routes/projects.ts:318-319, api/src/routes/comments.ts:22,60-61,143-144,230-231, api/src/routes/workspaces.ts:214,389,490,591,673,861
findings.evidence: Corrected non-null count for api is 288 sites (production, excluding 2 comment false positives and 4 test-file hits); 236 of those — 82% — are literally `req.userId!` or `req.workspaceId!`. The tracked script metric reports only 42 because the bundled regex's bracket expression is parsed literally by BSD grep (see Methodology), which under-counts by ~6.8x; the pattern is kept unchanged for compare-mode reproducibility.
findings.hypothesis: The auth middleware guarantees both fields after `requireAuth`, but the global Request augmentation must mark them optional because unauthenticated routes share the same type. Every authenticated handler therefore re-asserts. There is no `AuthenticatedRequest` type narrowing the fields to required after the middleware runs.
findings.estimatedImpact: Fixing one type declaration (an `AuthenticatedRequest` interface, or a typed middleware handler wrapper) retires 236 of the 321 corrected non-null assertions in one edit — ~15% of all tracked violations. Beyond the count: today a route registered without `requireAuth` compiles identically to one with it, so a middleware-ordering mistake sends `undefined` into SQL as a user/workspace id instead of failing to compile. That is an authorization-scoping risk, not just hygiene.

findings.title: The shared/ type contract is bypassed — 46 exported types, adopted by 13 of 198 web files, with ~40 duplicate local model declarations
findings.location: shared/src/types/*.ts (46 exported types); duplicates at web/src/hooks/useProjectsQuery.ts:8, web/src/components/ProjectCombobox.tsx:6, web/src/components/sidebars/ProjectSidebar.tsx:26, web/src/components/BulkActionBar.tsx:15, web/src/hooks/useWeeksQuery.ts:10, web/src/components/sidebars/WeekSidebar.tsx:27, web/src/components/AccountabilityGrid.tsx:8, web/src/lib/api.ts:5, and ~32 more
findings.evidence: `grep -rl "from '@ship/shared'"` matches 13 of 198 web/src files and 13 of 109 api/src files. Meanwhile grep for top-level `interface|type (Project|Issue|Sprint|Week|Program|Person|WikiDocument|UnifiedDocument|ApiResponse)` finds ~40 independent declarations in web/src alone: Project x5, Sprint x6, Program x6, Person x5, Issue x4, Week x3, WikiDocument x4. web/src/lib/api.ts:5 redeclares `interface ApiResponse<T>` although shared/src/types/api.ts:2 already exports `ApiResponse<T = unknown>` — the local copy has no default and no shared ApiError. shared itself is clean (0 `any`, 5 `as`), so the types are good; they are simply not used.
findings.hypothesis: Each feature was built by declaring the shape it needed at the point of use rather than importing from shared/, because the API responses those shapes describe are themselves untyped (TS-2) — there was no authoritative type to import from. The result is that the compiler validates each component against its own private guess at the contract, and cross-boundary drift is structurally undetectable.
findings.estimatedImpact: Consolidating on shared/ is the only way TS-2's typed row interfaces actually reach the frontend; done together, a backend field rename becomes a frontend compile error. Low direct violation-count payoff, high correctness payoff, and it is a prerequisite for the DB->API->UI chain to be checked end to end.

findings.title: No ESLint anywhere in the repo — `pnpm lint` is a silent no-op, so nothing prevents these counts from growing
findings.location: package.json:25 (`"lint": "pnpm --recursive run lint"`); no `lint` script in web/package.json, api/package.json, or shared/package.json
findings.evidence: No `.eslintrc*` or `eslint.config.*` file exists anywhere outside node_modules (verified with find across the tree). None of the three workspace packages defines a `lint` script, so the root recursive `lint` matches zero targets and exits 0. There is therefore no `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any`, `no-non-null-assertion`, `no-unsafe-assignment`, or `ban-ts-comment` rule in force, in CI or locally. The pre-commit hook chain (husky + `comply opensource` per CLAUDE.md) covers compliance, not type hygiene.
findings.hypothesis: Type-checking via `tsc --noEmit` was treated as sufficient static analysis. But tsc cannot flag an explicit `any` — `any` is legal TypeScript — so the entire violation class this audit measures is invisible to the only gate in place.
findings.estimatedImpact: Does not reduce the current count, but it is the ratchet: without it, any 25% reduction achieved will regress. Adding typescript-eslint with the four rules above set to `error` for new code (and a baseline suppression file for the existing 1535) is what makes the improvement durable. Note the no-op `lint` script also means the root `pnpm lint` reports success in CI while checking nothing.

findings.title: `as any` used to silence type mismatches on a destructive bulk mutation and on a SQL parameter
findings.evidence: Projects.tsx:220 `await updateProject(id, { archived_at: new Date().toISOString() } as any)` inside `handleBulkArchive`, and :233 `await updateProject(id, { archived_at: null } as any)` in the Undo handler. `updateProject` is typed `(id: string, updates: Partial<Project>) => Promise<Project | null>` (web/src/contexts/ProjectsContext.tsx:21) and `archived_at: string | null` IS a member of Project (web/src/hooks/useProjectsQuery.ts:~36) — so both assertions are currently unnecessary and purely defeat the check. api/src/routes/issues.ts:155 `params.push(states as any)` pushes a `string[]` into the SQL parameter array for an `= ANY($n)` clause; the assertion hides the element-type mismatch. These 3 sites are, with FileAttachment.tsx:139, the entire production `as any` population: 154 of the 158 `as any` occurrences are in test files (api 150 of 151, web 4 of 7).
findings.hypothesis: Copy-paste of a defensive assertion that was needed before `archived_at` was added to the Project interface, never removed. The issues.ts case is a genuine modelling gap: the `params` array is typed for scalars but pg legitimately accepts arrays for `= ANY`.
findings.estimatedImpact: Small count (3 sites) but disproportionate risk placement: it is on a bulk-archive path that mutates many records at once, and its Undo. Because the assertion is unnecessary today, it will silently absorb a real mismatch the first time the Project model changes — exactly the failure mode `as any` is dangerous for. Deleting the two web assertions is a zero-risk change; issues.ts needs the params array typed `(string | string[] | number)[]`.

findings.title: 68% of flagged sites are in test files, where `as any` mocks decouple tests from the shapes they claim to verify
findings.location: api/src/__tests__/transformIssueLinks.test.ts (37 sites), api/src/services/accountability.test.ts (32), api/src/__tests__/auth.test.ts (24), api/src/__tests__/activity.test.ts (21), api/src/routes/issues-history.test.ts (20), api/src/routes/projects.test.ts (17), api/src/routes/iterations.test.ts (9)
findings.evidence: 176 of 260 sites matching the script's combined pattern are in `*.test.*` / `__tests__` files. 154 of the 158 `as any` occurrences repo-wide are test-only — e.g. `vi.mocked(pool.query).mock.calls[0]![1] as any[]` (transformIssueLinks.test.ts:189) and `expect((editor.commands as any).setFileAttachment)` (web FileAttachment.test.ts:70-71). These are the top 6 entries in the raw density ranking, which is why the raw ranking is misleading about where risk lives.
findings.hypothesis: Mocking `pg`'s pool and TipTap's editor requires constructing partial objects; without factory helpers that return properly-typed partials, `as any` is the shortest path.
findings.estimatedImpact: Low blast radius on its own — but it means a route can change its response shape and its own unit test still compiles and passes, so these tests provide less regression protection than their count suggests. Mechanically the largest single reduction available: replacing these with typed mock factories is ~10% of all tracked violations. Per the skill's improvement rule this only counts if the mocks get real types, not `unknown`.

findings.title: web build and script files are never type-checked
findings.evidence: web's only tsconfig includes `src` only, and `web/tsconfig.node.json` — the conventional Vite companion config that would cover build tooling — does not exist (verified: No such file or directory). So `pnpm type-check` and the `tsc && vite build` step both skip vite.config.ts and web/scripts/. The `generate:icon-types` script (web/package.json) that generates the icon name union type is itself unchecked.
findings.hypothesis: The Vite React-TS template's split tsconfig (app + node) was partially removed; the app half survived and the node half was deleted rather than maintained.
findings.estimatedImpact: Hygiene. Build-config regressions surface as Vite runtime failures rather than compile errors, and the icon type generator — which produces types the rest of web depends on — is the least-checked file in the package. Adding a tsconfig.node.json is a few lines and closes the last untyped corner of the frontend.
